columns.label: Name
columns.desc: The project's name.

columns.label: Website
columns.desc: The project's official website.

columns.label: Repository
columns.desc: The project's GitHub repository, written as owner/name.

columns.label: License
columns.desc: The open-source license as reported by GitHub, for example MIT or Apache-2.0.

columns.label: Main language
columns.desc: The main programming language of the code, as reported by GitHub.

columns.label: GitHub stars
columns.desc: How many people have starred the repository on GitHub.

columns.label: Last code change
columns.desc: Date of the most recent commit to the repository.

columns.label: Latest release
columns.desc: Version name of the newest release published on GitHub.

columns.label: Latest release date
columns.desc: Date the newest GitHub release was published.

columns.label: Needs Docker
columns.desc: Yes when the documented install requires Docker.

columns.label: Where it runs
columns.desc: Whether you run it on your own machine, the vendor runs it for you, or both are possible.

columns.label: Pricing model
columns.desc: How the software itself is paid for, such as free open source or a subscription.

columns.label: Software price ($)
columns.desc: What the software itself costs and how often you pay it; $0 for free open source.

columns.label: Software price per month ($/month)
columns.desc: The software price in US dollars per month, calculated from the Software price column: monthly prices as is, yearly prices divided by 12, $0 stays $0, and other one-time prices are left empty.

columns.label: Hosted plan offered
columns.desc: Yes when the vendor offers to run it for you as a hosted service.

columns.label: Hosted plan from ($/month)
columns.desc: Monthly price of the cheapest hosted plan, in US dollars.

columns.label: Hosted plan up to ($/month)
columns.desc: Monthly price of the most expensive listed hosted plan, in US dollars.

columns.label: Free plan
columns.desc: Yes when there is a $0 plan or a free usage allowance.

columns.label: AI usage fees
columns.desc: How AI model usage is charged: not at all, passed through at cost, or with a markup.

columns.label: AI usage markup (%)
columns.desc: The percentage the vendor adds on top of the model provider's price.

columns.label: Vendor AI plan from ($/month)
columns.desc: Monthly price of the cheapest subscription to AI models sold by the vendor itself, such as OpenCode Go.

columns.label: Vendor AI plan up to ($/month)
columns.desc: Monthly price of the most expensive subscription to AI models sold by the vendor itself.

columns.label: Flat fee ($)
columns.desc: A fixed fee in US dollars, charged once per the unit shown in the Flat fee charged per column.

columns.label: Flat fee charged per
columns.desc: What the flat fee is charged on, such as each $20 credit top-up or each active agent per month.

columns.label: Which AI models
columns.desc: Which AI models you can use, one of: the vendor's own models only; many models through the vendor's account; any OpenAI-compatible service; your keys, only for providers the app already lists.
columns.extract_hint: first_party_only = only the vendor's own models; aggregator = many labs through one account of the vendor; byo_any_openai_compatible = any base URL + key + model id; byo_listed_providers_only = your keys, but only for providers it lists

columns.label: Built-in AI providers
columns.desc: AI model providers it supports out of the box.

columns.label: Number of built-in AI providers
columns.desc: How many providers are listed, counted from the Built-in AI providers column.

columns.label: Runs local models
columns.desc: Yes when it can use AI models running on your own computer, for example through Ollama.

columns.label: Any OpenAI-compatible service
columns.desc: Yes when you can point it at any service that speaks the OpenAI API by giving a URL and key.

columns.label: Any Anthropic-compatible service
columns.desc: Yes when you can point it at any service that speaks the Anthropic API by giving a URL and key.

columns.label: Uses coding-agent tools
columns.desc: Command-line coding agents, such as Claude Code or Codex, that it can use as its engine.

columns.label: AI models included
columns.desc: Yes when the vendor itself provides access to AI models, free or paid, so you do not need your own key.

columns.label: Models offered by vendor
columns.desc: How many AI models the vendor's own cloud offers.

columns.label: Use your own keys
columns.desc: Yes when you can use your own API keys or AI subscriptions.

columns.label: Chat apps
columns.desc: The apps and channels you can talk to it through.

columns.label: Phone chat apps
columns.desc: Yes when the Chat apps column includes Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage or SMS.

columns.label: Desktop app
columns.desc: Yes when it has an installable desktop app.

columns.label: Conversation style
columns.desc: How conversations work, one of: One ongoing chat; Automatic sessions, shared memory; Sessions you manage, shared memory; Separate sessions, no shared memory.
columns.extract_hint: single_ongoing = one chat forever, no resets; auto_sessions_with_memory = harness resets/compacts sessions itself and memory carries over, user never manages sessions; manual_sessions_with_memory = user starts/picks sessions, memory carries over; sessions_only = user manages sessions, no cross-session memory

columns.label: Shortens long chats itself
columns.desc: Yes when it summarizes or trims a conversation by itself once it gets too long.

columns.label: Memory stored as
columns.desc: Where its memory is kept, one or more of: Markdown files; SQLite database; Vector store; Knowledge graph. When the source says several are used but does not name them, the value is "More than one kind" instead of a guess.

columns.label: Memory shared by
columns.desc: Who shares one memory, one of: One session; One bot; One user; All bots.

columns.label: Memory writer
columns.desc: Who writes to memory: only you, the agent when you ask, the agent on its own, or a background process.

columns.label: Memory cleanup
columns.desc: How old memory is tidied: not at all, by summarizing, by merging duplicates, or by removing stale items.

columns.label: Memory cleanup every (hours)
columns.desc: How often the memory cleanup runs, in hours.

columns.label: Memory recall
columns.desc: How memory gets back into a conversation: all of it every time, keyword search, meaning-based search, or a tool the agent calls.

columns.label: Memory size limit (tokens)
columns.desc: The maximum size of memory, in tokens.

columns.label: Memory kept when chat is shortened
columns.desc: Yes when memory survives after a long chat is summarized or trimmed.

columns.label: Memory kept after a fresh start
columns.desc: Yes when memory survives after you start a new chat.

columns.label: Keeps a profile of you
columns.desc: Yes when it stores facts about you in a separate profile.

columns.label: Keeps a project log
columns.desc: Yes when it keeps a running log for each project.

columns.label: Saves skills
columns.desc: Yes when it stores reusable skills or step-by-step procedures.

columns.label: Memory readable by you
columns.desc: Yes when memory is stored in a form you can read, such as text files.

columns.label: Memory editable by you
columns.desc: Yes when you can edit what it remembers.

columns.label: Memory exportable
columns.desc: Yes when you can export its memory to take it elsewhere.

columns.label: Memory history kept
columns.desc: Yes when earlier versions of memory are kept, for example in git.

columns.label: Writes its own memory
columns.desc: Yes when the agent or a background process writes memory, calculated from the Memory writer column.

columns.label: Learns about you
columns.desc: Yes when it learns your preferences on its own over time.

columns.label: Writes its own skills
columns.desc: Yes when it creates new reusable skills by itself.

columns.label: Scheduled tasks
columns.desc: Yes when you can schedule tasks to run at set times.

columns.label: Schedules its own tasks
columns.desc: Yes when the agent can create scheduled tasks for itself.

columns.label: Helper agents
columns.desc: Yes when it can start helper agents that work in parallel or in the background.

columns.label: Agent teams
columns.desc: Yes when several named agents with different roles can work together.

columns.label: Messages you first
columns.desc: Yes when it can send you a message without being asked.

columns.label: MCP tools
columns.desc: Yes when it can use tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

columns.label: Memory use when idle (MB)
columns.desc: How much RAM it uses while idle, in megabytes.

columns.label: Install size (MB)
columns.desc: Disk space of the installed program, in megabytes.

columns.label: Summary
columns.desc: A short description written from the project's own pages.

columns.label: Tags
columns.desc: Short topic keywords for search.

columns.label: Notes
columns.desc: Our editorial notes about this entry.
